answer: Admission rests on a serial an outside registrar signs to one public key - say a licensed domain. A vault on the ledger holds claimed serials: a second key citing an occupied one is refused, and a moved claim needs a new signature. Each epoch the beacon asks the registrar whether a sampled filing stands; no answer retires that key and burns its pay. A key clones for free, a filing does not: N identities need N real registrations with their own fees and contacts, so cost grows with N. One island holds one claimant; the public mesa of serials exposes duplicates before rewards split.
